name: Evaluation of scientific evidence and sources of error

questions.q: What is the distinction between random errors and systematic errors in biological experiments?
a: Random errors cause unpredictable scatter around the true value and can be reduced by replicates; systematic errors shift all measurements consistently in one direction due to faulty calibration
Random errors are caused by teachers; systematic errors are caused by students
Random errors are intentional; systematic errors are accidental
There is no scientific difference between them

questions.q: How can an investigator effectively minimize the impact of random errors during an enzyme practical trial?
a: Perform only a single trial and guess the rest
Repeat the experiment multiple times under identical conditions and calculate a mean
Change the independent variable randomly
Ignore all data that does not fit expectations

questions.q: What is a systematic error?
a: A random fluctuation in room lighting
An error caused by student fatigue
A consistent, repeatable error resulting from faulty equipment calibration or flawed experimental setup (e.g., a balance reading 0.5g when empty)
A calculation mistake made on a calculator

questions.q: In an experiment measuring gas production from yeast respiration, what is a major potential source of systematic error if not checked?
a: The student's handwriting style
The color of the laboratory walls
The brand of stopwatch used
A gas syringe sticking or leaking gas around the plunger, causing every volume reading to be systematically too low

questions.q: What does the term 'reliability' mean in scientific practical investigations?
a: The extent to which repeated measurements under identical conditions yield consistent, similar results (showing low random error)
Whether the experiment proves the hypothesis correct
How expensive the laboratory equipment is
Whether the experiment took less than ten minutes

questions.q: What is meant by the 'validity' of an experimental method?
a: Whether the results are printed in ink
Whether the experiment actually measures what it sets out to measure by successfully controlling all extraneous variables
How many students participated in the practical
Whether the graph paper is green or white

questions.q: Why is it important to evaluate an experimental procedure critically after completing a practical?
a: To waste time before lunch
To find excuses to fail the class
To identify limitations, sources of error, and suggest realistic improvements that enhance future accuracy and reliability
To prove that science is never certain

questions.q: If an experiment investigating osmosis in potato cylinders shows wide variation between three replicate samples at the same concentration, what should be evaluated about the method?
a: The potato cylinders were likely cut to inconsistent sizes and surface areas, indicating poor control of variables
The balance was too accurate
The room was too cold
The sucrose solution was magical

questions.q: What is an anomalous result?
a: A data point that does not fit the general pattern or trend of the rest of the dataset (an outlier)
The exact median of a table
The highest possible score achievable
The independent variable value

questions.q: How should an anomalous result identified during data analysis be handled properly?
a: Include it in the mean calculation to keep numbers high
Investigate potential experimental errors, repeat the measurement if possible, and exclude the anomaly from final mean calculations
Change all other data points to match the anomaly
Throw away the entire scientific report

questions.q: When evaluating an investigation on photosynthesis where pondweed was illuminated by a lamp, what unmeasured variable could have acted as an uncontrolled confounding factor?
a: The student's eye color
The brand of glass beaker
Changes in water temperature caused by heat radiated from the lamp
The day of the week

questions.q: What is precision in scientific measurement?
a: How close a measurement is to the true, actual value in nature
Whether the experiment is published in a journal
How fast the data is collected
The closeness of agreement between independent measurements obtained under stipulated conditions (reflecting instrument resolution)

questions.q: Why is parallax error considered an avoidable human error when reading a measuring cylinder?
a: It occurs when the observer's eye is not positioned directly level with the liquid meniscus, leading to misreading of volume
It is caused by magnetic fields in the room
It happens only in total darkness
It is caused by broken glass

questions.q: How can parallax error be prevented when taking readings from a thermometer or graduated pipette?
a: Read the instrument from across the laboratory
Ensure your eye is positioned directly perpendicular (eye-level) to the meniscus or liquid level
Tilt the apparatus at a 45-degree angle
Use a magnifying glass from below

questions.q: What is a limitation in an experimental design?
a: The number of pages in a notebook
The name of the researcher
A restriction or flaw in the method, apparatus, or scope that limits the certainty or generalizability of conclusions
The brightness of the ceiling lights

questions.q: If student data points on a graph are widely scattered around the line of best fit, what does this evaluation imply about the technique used?
a: The technique had high precision
The equipment was state-of-the-art
The experiment was conducted in a vacuum
The technique suffered from high random error and poor experimental control

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of suggesting practical improvements during an evaluation question in an exam?
a: To propose specific, realistic modifications that reduce identified errors or improve control of variables
To criticize the teacher personally
To invent new chemical elements
To make the experiment cost more money

questions.q: Why might an experiment investigating enzyme activity yield lower product formation than expected from textbook theory?
a: Enzymes were working at maximum efficiency
The enzyme preparation may have degraded, or incubation times were insufficient
The room was too bright
The glassware was too clean

questions.q: When evaluating a field study estimating dandelion population using quadrats, what limitation could lead to an inaccurate total population estimate?
a: Using too many quadrats randomly
Counting every single plant meticulously
Placing quadrats in only one biased corner of the field rather than truly randomly across the whole habitat
Recording data in a table with units

questions.q: What does a low percentage error in a practical result indicate about the experimental procedure?
a: The calculations were done in pencil
The student cheated on the homework
The equipment was broken
High accuracy, meaning the experimental value is very close to the accepted theoretical value

questions.q: What is the key difference between accuracy and precision?
a: Accuracy is how close a measurement is to the true value; precision is how close repeated measurements are to each other
Accuracy relates to numbers; precision relates to words
Accuracy is random; precision is systematic
There is no difference between them

questions.q: Why is it poor scientific practice to state 'human error' as the primary source of error in an evaluation without further specification?
a: Humans are legally protected from criticism
It is too vague; scientists must specify the exact procedural flaw (e.g., parallax error when reading volume or reaction time delay in stopping a stopwatch)
Humans do not participate in experiments
It takes too many words to write

questions.q: How can the precision of a measuring cylinder be improved during a practical?
a: Use a smaller capacity measuring cylinder or a pipette/burette with finer scale graduations
Fill it to the brim with water
Paint the outside black
Read it while running

questions.q: What is the significance of identifying and controlling extraneous variables in an investigation?
a: It makes the report look complicated
It ensures that the experiment finishes quickly
It allows the student to go home early
It ensures that the dependent variable changes are caused solely by the independent variable, establishing validity
